data.title: Where every number comes from
data.sub: Sourced figures link to their source. Everything else is labelled as an assumption or illustrative.

extraSources.title: Solar irradiance tiers (InfraLens; MNRE Solar Atlas + Solargis)
PM Surya Ghar 50 lakh homes, 14.8 GW (Mercom, Aug 2026)
India boundary: DataMeet maps, Survey of India state boundaries (CC BY 4.0)

engine.monthly: Energy balance uses each month's average day (hourly solar shape from day length), not hourly weather data. Estimate from monthly averages, not a guarantee.
engine.storm: The worst solar month includes one low-sun spell of 1–5 days with solar at 35% of that month's average, followed by recovery days.
engine.autonomy: Battery = night-time demand × autonomy (1 day at 1 storm day, rising to 2 days at 5) ÷ (depth of discharge × round-trip efficiency). LFP: 80% DoD, 90% RTE.
engine.greedy: PV starts at demand ÷ (worst-month GHI × 0.75) × 1.1, then PV (+6%) or battery (+10%) is added, whichever removes more shortfall per rupee, until the worst month meets ≥99%.
engine.diesel: Solar + diesel: PV on the average month, one night of battery, and a generator (peak ÷ 0.8 × 1.2 kVA) that covers any shortfall at 3.4 kWh/litre.
engine.hydro: Small hydro only where potential is medium or high; three sizes are tried (30/60/90% of average load, capped by site potential) and the cheapest is kept. Dry months follow a seasonal flow curve reduced by the slider.
engine.wind: Wind only where a 20 m small turbine reaches ≥9% capacity factor (Rayleigh distribution, 3/11/25 m/s power curve, 15% losses). Three sizes are tried.
engine.geothermal: Geothermal is pilot-stage only in India: shown as potential, never sized.
engine.growth: Demand grows by the slider; capacity is topped up every 5 years. Solar degrades 0.5%/yr; the 1.1 margin covers it.
engine.baseline: Diesel-only baseline: generator + fuel + ₹2/kWh O&M. Grid baseline: tariff escalating 3%/yr. Payback is the first year cumulative cost falls below the baseline.
engine.impact: Impact score: CO₂ avoided 30%, diesel saved 25%, homes served per ₹ crore 25%, cost-efficiency (1/LCOE) 20%, min–max normalised across all 50 districts using a default village design. Grid factor 0.71 kg CO₂/kWh is an assumption to verify with CEA.

data.districtsBody: All 50 districts carry ILLUSTRATIVE monthly solar (GHI) and wind (50 m) values from published tiers (MNRE Solar Atlas + Solargis long-term averages), with a monsoon dip for monsoon regions and a winter dip for Himalayan districts. Population and demand are rough estimates. Drop NASA POWER climatology CSVs into /data-raw and run `npm run import:nasa` to replace them with real values.
data.boundaryBody: The India outline and state lines come from DataMeet's Survey of India based state boundaries (States/Admin2), which include all of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh as per the official map of India. They were simplified for the web with mapshaper. Please verify against the Survey of India's official political map before publishing.

impact.note: Each metric is min–max normalised across the 50 districts, then weighted. Homes per ₹ crore = 100 homes ÷ capex in crore ({{capex}} = 1 crore). Illustrative data.
